title: A headless run can answer a push or secrets gate as the operator: the --by operator deny matches one argument order only
goal: when KB_HEADLESS_RUNNER is set (every headless runner), backlog.py answer and kbdecide.py refuse `--by operator`, `--confirm` without `--by`, and `--record` with `--by operator`, whatever the argument order or option abbreviation (exit 2, item unchanged, the message names the variable); the RUNNER_DENY rule in autopilot.py stays as a second layer but no test or doc treats it as the guard; planted-failure tests run the reordered form (`answer --by operator ID GATE ...`), the abbreviation (`--b operator`) and `--confirm` with the variable set, plus the positives with it unset (the operator-present manager session keeps recording interview answers with --by operator); found by the SP-itmjxudu review

run: set -e; d=$(mktemp -d); git clone -q "$PWD" "$d/r"; cd "$d/r"; f=$(grep -L '"sprint"' kb/_self/backlog/BG-*.json | head -1); id=$(basename "$f" .json); python3 _tools/backlog.py gate add "$id" --kind blocking --id pushgate --question "Push the commits to the public remote?" --option yes --option no --recommendation yes --do "yes=true" --do "no=true" >/dev/null; if KB_HEADLESS_RUNNER=1 python3 _tools/backlog.py answer --by operator --answer yes "$id" pushgate >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 1; fi
